generator_assessments.assessment: The presence of acid-fast bacilli is a definitive modality finding for lupus vulgaris, a form of cutaneous tuberculosis.
The presence of non-caseating granulomas, as suggested by the diffuse infiltrate of foamy histiocytes, and lymphadenopathy are consistent with sarcoidosis.

raw_support_spans.text: Diffuse infiltrate of foamy histiocytes in the dermis (hematoxylin-eosin stain)
enlarged axillary, cervical, and inguinal lymph nodes and enlarged spleen

generator_assessments.assessment: The significantly elevated rheumatoid factor and imaging findings of synovitis, tenosynovitis, and bone erosions are characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis.

raw_support_spans.text: X-ray and joint ultrasound showed: osteoarthritis, synovitis, flexor tendon tenosynovitis, and bone erosions

decisive_items: Diffuse infiltrate of foamy histiocytes in the dermis (hematoxylin-eosin stain)
Multiple asymptomatic nodules without ulceration on upper arms
response.rationale: The presence of numerous acid-fast bacilli with foamy histiocytes is definitive for a mycobacterial infection, and among the options, lupus vulgaris (cutaneous tuberculosis) is the only one that fits. Sarcoidosis and rheumatoid arthritis do not explain the AFB-positive biopsy.

rejected.why: Sarcoidosis typically shows non-caseating granulomas, not foamy histiocytes with numerous AFB; the AFB finding is incompatible.
Rheumatoid arthritis explains the joint symptoms and elevated RF but cannot account for the AFB-positive skin nodules or foamy histiocyte infiltrate.
